heading: Commissioner of Public Records
blurb: Selected government records from 1750 to 1783 that mention free and enslaved Black people in Nova Scotia.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: Commissioner of Public Records Collection — Black Refugees
blurb: Original copies and transcripts of records about Black immigration and settlement in Nova Scotia, from the end of the Revolutionary War in 1783 to emancipation in 1838.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: The Book of Negroes
blurb: A register of about 3,000 Black refugees who sailed from New York to Nova Scotia in 1783. This is a digital presentation of a document whose original is held by The National Archives (UK).
ref: Sir Guy Carleton Papers no. 10427, The National Archives (UK), PRO 30/55/100

curated.access_note: Digital presentation on the Nova Scotia Archives site. The source cites the original as held by The National Archives, Kew.

heading: Nova Scotia House of Assembly
blurb: Petitions and correspondence in which African Nova Scotians asked the legislature for relief, support for farming and fishing, schools and roads.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: Nova Scotia Lands and Forests
blurb: Crown land records from 1786 to 1824, including land granted to Black settlers and their original petitions about land title.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: William Hall, VC
blurb: Records about William Hall (1827 to 1904), the first Black person and first Nova Scotian to receive the Victoria Cross, including commemoration and the search for his missing medals.

curated.access_note: Online exhibit on the Nova Scotia Archives website.

heading: No. 2 Construction Battalion: Nominal Roll
blurb: The March 1917 nominal roll of officers, non-commissioned officers and men of No. 2 Construction Battalion, the only battalion of Black soldiers raised in Canada in the First World War.

curated.access_note: Digitized roll on the Nova Scotia Archives website.

heading: Viola Irene Desmond
blurb: Court documents, period newspaper coverage and background on Viola Desmond, who challenged racial discrimination in 1946.

curated.access_note: Online exhibit with digitized legal documents and newspaper coverage.

heading: Africville
blurb: Newspaper clippings and correspondence about the expropriation of Africville and the relocation of its residents between 1962 and 1969, with an 1854 petition and national magazine coverage.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: Bob Brooks' Photographic Portrait of Africville
blurb: An online exhibit of nearly 60 photographs by photojournalist Bob Brooks showing Africville in the 1960s, including a 1962 public meeting at Seaview African United Baptist Church.

curated.access_note: Online exhibit. Photographs are by Bob Brooks and held by the Nova Scotia Archives; ROOTS shows no images because thumbnails need permission.

heading: Black Horizon - Black United Front
blurb: A video playlist of Black Horizon, a talk show on Dartmouth Cable Television from 1976 to 1983 about African Nova Scotian topics, run as one of the Black United Front's initiatives.

curated.access_note: Hosted as a video playlist linked from the Nova Scotia Archives page.

heading: Lorne White family
blurb: Records about Lorne White and his family: his music and acting career, his sister Portia White's achievements, and their father Rev. Captain William A. White of No. 2 Construction Battalion.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: Jones Clayton family
blurb: Photographs, recordings, correspondence and documents of two families prominent in the African Nova Scotian United Baptist Church community, with material on Viola Desmond, Rev. Dr. William P. Oliver and Pearleen Oliver.

curated.access_note: Selected items are digitized and searchable on the Nova Scotia Archives website; originals are held by the Archives.

heading: Nova Scotia Women's Oral History Project: Pearleen Oliver Interview
blurb: A summer 1992 interview with Dr. Pearleen Oliver, human rights advocate, historian and choir director, recorded for an oral history project begun in 1989 by Marjory Whitelaw.

curated.access_note: Item page on the Nova Scotia Archives website.

heading: Preliminary Report of the Officials' Committee on Black Communities in Nova Scotia
blurb: An April 1985 report by the Nova Scotia Executive Council's Officials' Committee on Black Communities, digitized from the Archives library.
ref: Nova Scotia Archives Library HN 1100 N935 B631

curated.access_note: Digitized from the Nova Scotia Archives Library.

heading: List of Black people settled on Block Letter A, Preston (?)
blurb: A settlement list from the Black Refugees series with page images and a transcript. The source title marks the place name as uncertain.
ref: Commissioner of Public Records, Black Refugees series, RG 1 volume 419 number 92

curated.access_note: Item page with page images and a transcript.

heading: Black Loyalists in Canada: Autonomy, Advocacy, Community, Legacy
blurb: A collection of documents on Black Loyalists who arrived in Nova Scotia from the United States in the 1780s and their descendants. News coverage in March 2026 says it is jointly held by four institutions and was added to the Canada Memory of the World Register.

curated.access_note: Digitized content is available through Nova Scotia Archives pages. Other holders are listed in the record.
curated.source_note: Joint holding and UNESCO listing are reported by CP24 (21 March 2026), not by the archives page itself.
